examples.en: The police arrested the thief.

examples.ko: 경찰은 그 남자를 곧 체포할 거예요.
examples.en: The police will arrest that man soon.
I watched a movie about arresting a criminal.
They took the arrested person to the police station.

examples.ko: 경찰이 길에서 그 사람을 체포하고 이름을 물었어요.
examples.en: The police arrested him on the street and asked his name.

examples.ko: 아직 체포하지 못해서 계속 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: They have not been able to arrest him yet, so they keep looking.

explain: '잡다'는 누구나 쓰지만 '체포하다'는 경찰이나 수사 기관이 할 때만 써요. 친구를 붙잡았을 때는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스에서는 '검거하다'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 경찰 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I heard that the police arrested the thief.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 들은 소식을 전할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a way to pass on news you heard from someone else.

phrases.en: The police have not been able to arrest the criminal yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡으려 했지만 잡지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means someone tried to arrest but could not.

phrases.en: The police tried to arrest the man.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체포를 시작하려는 순간이나 시도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for the moment of attempting an arrest.

explain_en: Active, legal and formal: police arrest a suspect (도둑을 체포하다) Anyone can use '잡다', but '체포하다' is only for police or investigators. You would not use it when you grab a friend. In the news, '검거하다' is used similarly, but it is the police's own word.

examples.en: The police questioned the suspect all night.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 형사가 취조하는 장면이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The scene in the drama where the detective interrogates someone was impressive.
Please don't ask me as if you're interrogating me to tell the truth.

examples.ko: 친구가 어제 어디 갔냐고 저를 취조해요.
examples.en: My friend grills me about where I went yesterday.

examples.ko: 취조받는 사람도 변호사를 부를 수 있어요.
examples.en: A person being interrogated can also call a lawyer.

examples.ko: 엄마가 성적표를 보고 저를 취조하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My mom looked at my report card and started grilling me.

explain: 경찰이나 검사가 혐의가 있는 사람에게 꼬치꼬치 캐묻는 장면에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 친구나 가족이 집요하게 물어볼 때 '취조하는 것 같다'고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. 수사 뉴스에서는 '조사하다'라는 말도 같이 써요.

phrases.en: He was interrogated all night at the police station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취조를 당하는 사람의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person being questioned.

phrases.en: It was quiet and scary inside the interrogation room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취조가 이루어지는 방을 말하고 드라마에도 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The room where an interrogation takes place, often seen in dramas.

phrases.en: Why are you asking me like you're interrogating me?
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족이 너무 꼬치꼬치 물을 때 농담처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used jokingly when a friend or family member asks too many detailed questions.

explain_en: Police questioning a suspect closely, often long and harsh; crime news. It is used for scenes where police or prosecutors press a suspect with detailed questions. In daily life people jokingly say '취조하는 것 같다' when a friend or family member keeps asking pushy questions. In investigation news, '조사하다' is also used.

t90.ax: The police questioned the suspect all night.

en: to invade; to wage aggression against

examples.en: In the old days, foreign enemies often invaded our country.

examples.ko: 적이 침략해 오자 사람들은 성으로 피했어요.
examples.en: When the enemy invaded, people took refuge in the castle.
In the movie, aliens invade Earth.

examples.ko: 다른 나라를 침략하는 것은 국제법 위반이에요.
examples.en: Invading another country violates international law.
It came out that they had made plans to invade.
That region was invaded several times.

explain: 다른 나라를 힘으로 공격해 들어가는 나쁜 일에 써요. 남의 집이나 건물에 몰래 들어가는 것은 '침입하다'예요. 공격을 받은 쪽은 '침략을 당하다', '침략당하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: That country was invaded many times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공격을 받은 쪽에서 말하는 피해 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the victim who was invaded.

phrases.en: That king invaded the neighboring country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나라를 침략하다'처럼 '을/를'로 대상을 받아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The target takes the object marker 을/를.

phrases.example: 옛날에 그 나라가 우리를 침략한 적이 있어요.
phrases.en: That country invaded us long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 적이 있다'로 지난 경험이나 역사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-ㄴ 적이 있다' talks about past events or history.

explain_en: Formal, invading to conquer or plunder; history and news. It describes attacking and entering another country by force, so it carries a negative tone. Sneaking into someone's house or building is '침입하다'. The side that gets attacked says '침략을 당하다' or '침략당하다'.

t90.ax: In the movie, aliens invade Earth.

examples.ko: 월급이 밀린 판국에 보너스는 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: With our pay overdue, we can't even dream of a bonus.
You're bringing up a trip in a situation like this?

examples.ko: 나라 경제가 어려운 판국이라 모두 조심해요.
examples.en: The national economy is in a tough spot, so everyone is careful.

examples.ko: 시험이 내일인 판국에 게임이 하고 싶어요?
examples.en: The exam is tomorrow and you want to play games?

examples.ko: 일이 이런 판국이 될 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't know things would end up in a state like this.

examples.ko: 판국을 보니 오늘은 일찍 퇴근하기 힘들겠어요.
examples.en: Looking at how things stand, leaving early today will be hard.

explain: '상황'과 비슷하지만 좋지 않은 일이 벌어진 형편에 주로 써요. '~ㄴ 판국에'로 많이 쓰고, 한숨이나 나무라는 느낌이 들어가요. 좋은 상황에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: How can you laugh in a situation like this?
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 상황에서 상대의 태도를 나무랄 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression used to scold someone's attitude in a bad situation.

phrases.en: You're going on a picnic with rain pouring down?
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 뒤에 붙여 좋지 않은 상황이 벌어지는 중에라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to a verb to mean in the middle of a bad situation.

phrases.en: I'm so worried now that things have turned out like this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 좋지 않게 흘러갔다고 한숨 쉬듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said with a sigh when things have turned out badly.

explain_en: It is similar to '상황' but is mostly used for a bad or troubling state of affairs. It often appears as '~ㄴ 판국에' and carries a sigh or a scolding tone. It is rarely used for good situations.

t90.ax: The exam is tomorrow and you want to play games?

examples.ko: 회사는 재판에서 패소해서 큰돈을 물어 줬어요.
examples.en: The company lost the trial and had to pay a large sum.
He lost in the first trial but decided to go to court again.

examples.ko: 가게 주인은 소송에서 패소할까 봐 걱정했어요.
examples.en: The shop owner was worried about losing the lawsuit.
If I lose the case, do I have to pay the legal costs too?
The lawyer said there is a high chance of losing the case.

examples.ko: 그는 두 번이나 패소하고도 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even after losing twice, he did not give up.

explain: 반대말은 '승소하다'예요. 보통 '재판에서/소송에서 패소하다'로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '소송에서 지다'라고도 해요. 법정이나 뉴스 같은 상황에만 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 소송에서 져서 돈을 물어 줘야 해요.
phrases.en: I lost the lawsuit, so I have to pay money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '패소하다'를 쉬운 동사 '지다'로 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer way to say 패소하다 using the common verb 지다.

phrases.en: The court ruled against the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판 결과를 말하는 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that often appears in news reporting trial results.

phrases.en: If you lose the case, you have to pay the legal costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-면'을 붙여서 재판에서 졌을 때의 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -면 it states the consequence of losing the case.

explain_en: Its opposite is '승소하다' (win a case). It is usually used as '재판에서/소송에서 패소하다', and in everyday talk people also say '소송에서 지다'. It only appears in court or news contexts.

examples.en: The prosecutor did not accept the ruling and appealed.
The result felt unfair, so I decided to appeal.
To appeal, you have to submit the documents first.
The company will appeal within a week.
A person who has appealed goes through the trial again.
Even if you appeal, the result may be the same.

explain: 1심 판결에 불복할 때 '항소하다'를 쓰고, 2심 뒤에 대법원으로 가는 건 '상고하다'예요. 보통 '판결에 항소하다'처럼 써요. 뉴스에서 '항소했다'로 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The lawyer said they would appeal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 뜻을 전할 때 '-겠다고'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -겠다고 to report an intention to do it in the future.

phrases.example: 양쪽 모두 항소하지 않아서 판결이 확정됐어요.
phrases.en: Neither side appealed, so the verdict became final.
phrases.nuance_ko: 항소를 안 해서 판결이 그대로 끝난다는 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news saying the verdict stands because no one appealed.

phrases.en: I felt wronged, so I filed an appeal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '항소하다'와 뜻이 같고 명사로 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 항소하다, expressed with the noun.

explain_en: You 항소하다 when you do not accept a first-trial ruling; going to the Supreme Court after the second trial is 상고하다. It is used like '판결에 항소하다'. In the news you often hear '항소했다'.

examples.ko: 바다 위에 빨간 부표가 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A red buoy is floating on the sea.

examples.ko: 어부들은 부표를 보고 그물 위치를 찾아요.
examples.en: Fishermen find where their nets are by looking at the buoy.
We are careful so the boat doesn't hit the buoy.
The buoy drifted far away because of the waves.
The angler stopped the boat next to the buoy.

examples.ko: 항구 근처에는 안전을 알리는 부표가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many buoys marking safety near the harbor.

explain: 바다나 강에 띄워서 위치나 위험한 곳을 알리는 물건이에요. 낚싯줄에 달린 '찌'와 비슷해 보이지만, 부표는 그물이나 항로를 표시하는 큰 표지를 말해요. 뉴스에서는 양식장 '스티로폼 부표' 이야기가 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The fisherman set a buoy afloat on the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부표를 설치하는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the act of setting a buoy in the water.

phrases.example: 배 근처에 노란 부표가 떠 있어요.
phrases.en: A yellow buoy is floating near the boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물 위에 떠 있는 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a buoy floating on the water.

phrases.en: Styrofoam buoys left in the sea are a problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in environmental news.

explain_en: Floating marker on the sea guiding ships. It is a float placed on the sea or a river to mark a position or a danger. It looks like a fishing '찌' (bobber), but a 부표 is a larger marker for nets or sea routes. In the news you often hear about styrofoam buoys at fish farms.

examples.en: I made a small house model with matchsticks.
I lit the candle with a single matchstick.
The matchstick got wet, so it won't light.
I picked up the matchstick that fell on the floor.
It is dangerous to give matchsticks to a child.
He is thin as a matchstick, so I'm worried.

explain: '성냥'은 전체를 말하고, '성냥개비'는 막대 하나를 가리킬 때 잘 어울려요. 요즘은 라이터를 더 많이 쓰지만, 만들기나 옛날이야기에서 아직 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: We made a fire with matches at the campsite.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성냥개비'는 막대 하나를, '성냥'은 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 성냥개비 is a single stick, while 성냥 refers to matches in general.

phrases.en: Please lend me just one matchstick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하나씩 셀 때 '한 개'를 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 한 개 to count them one by one.

phrases.en: I lit the match and lit the candle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불을 붙이는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the action of lighting it.

explain_en: '성냥' refers to matches in general, while '성냥개비' fits best when pointing to a single stick. Lighters are more common today, but matchsticks still come up in crafts and old stories.

examples.en: They turned the blower up high in the hot factory.

examples.ko: 송풍기가 고장 나서 환기가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: The blower is broken, so the ventilation isn't working well.

examples.ko: 터널 안에는 큰 송풍기가 여러 대 있어요.
examples.en: There are several big blowers inside the tunnel.
The blower is so loud that it's hard to talk.

examples.ko: 새 송풍기를 달았더니 공기가 잘 통해요.
examples.en: Since we installed a new blower, the air circulates well.

examples.ko: 송풍기를 켜 놓으면 곰팡이가 덜 생겨요.
examples.en: If you leave the blower on, less mold grows.

explain: 선풍기는 사람 쪽으로 바람을 보내는 가전이고, 송풍기는 주로 공장, 터널, 큰 건물에서 공기를 보내는 기계에 써요. 집에서 쓰는 바람 나오는 기계는 보통 선풍기라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The air was stuffy, so I turned on the blower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 작동시킬 때 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pairing for turning the machine on.

phrases.en: The blowers keep running inside the tunnel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 작동하고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the machine running.

phrases.en: The blower noise is too loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 기계의 소음을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the noise of large machines.

explain_en: A 선풍기 is a household fan that blows air toward people, while a 송풍기 is mainly a machine that moves air in factories, tunnels and large buildings. The machine at home that blows air is usually just called a 선풍기.

t90.ax: If you leave the blower on, less mold grows.

examples.ko: 산속에 낡은 움막이 한 채 있어요.
examples.en: There is one old hut in the mountains.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 땅을 파고 움막을 지었어요.
examples.en: People long ago dug into the ground and built dugout huts.
I went into a nearby hut to get out of the rain.
I spent one night in the hut and it was freezing.
They lived in a house like a dugout hut.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되기 전에 움막을 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: We have to fix the hut before winter comes.

explain: 땅을 파거나 낮게 지어서 위를 덮은, 허술하고 임시로 쓰는 집이에요. 옛날 생활이나 산속의 초라한 집을 이야기할 때 나와요. 작고 소박한 집을 말하는 '오두막'과 비슷하지만, 움막은 더 허름하고 낮은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The hunter built a hut in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간단하게 임시 집을 만든다는 뜻으로 '짓다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '짓다' to mean building a simple, temporary shelter.

phrases.example: 산 아래 움막집에서 할아버지가 혼자 살아요.
phrases.en: An old man lives alone in a hut at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '움막'에 '집'을 붙여 사는 곳이라는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '집' emphasizes that it's a place where someone lives.

phrases.en: I spent a night in a cabin in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움막보다 덜 허름하고, 작은 집을 가리켜 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less shabby than 움막 and used more often for any small cabin.

explain_en: It is a crude, temporary shelter dug into the ground or built low and covered over. It comes up when talking about life in the past or a shabby shelter in the mountains. It is similar to '오두막', a small simple cabin, but 움막 feels lower and more rundown.

examples.en: I sold the loot I got in the game at the shop.
When you defeat the boss, loot drops.

examples.ko: 그 박물관에는 전쟁에서 가져온 전리품이 있어요.
examples.en: That museum has spoils brought back from a war.

examples.ko: 여행 전리품으로 기념품을 한가득 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I brought back a lot of souvenirs as my trip's haul.
We decided to split the loot equally among team members.

examples.ko: 쇼핑 전리품을 침대 위에 펼쳐 놓았어요.
examples.en: I spread my shopping haul out on the bed.

explain: 원래는 전쟁에서 빼앗은 물건이지만, 요즘은 게임에서 얻는 아이템이나 쇼핑·여행에서 얻은 것을 장난스럽게 말할 때도 많이 써요. '트로피'는 상으로 받는 컵이라서 전리품과 달라요.

phrases.example: 쇼핑을 마치고 전리품을 한가득 챙겨서 집에 왔어요.
phrases.en: After shopping, I came home with a whole load of spoils.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑이나 여행에서 산 것을 장난스럽게 '전리품'이라고 부르며 챙길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Playfully calls things bought while shopping or traveling 'spoils'.

phrases.en: The party members divided the loot fairly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임에서 함께 얻은 아이템을 나눌 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in games when teammates split the items they won together.

phrases.example: 박물관에는 옛날 전쟁 전리품이 전시돼 있어요.
phrases.en: The museum displays spoils from old wars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 뜻인 전쟁에서 빼앗은 물건을 말할 때 '전쟁'을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 전쟁 in front to mean the original sense of goods seized in war.

explain_en: Things taken after winning; also playful for game rewards. Originally it means things taken in war, but these days it is also used playfully for items won in games or things gained from shopping or travel. A '트로피' is a cup given as a prize, so it is different from '전리품'.

examples.ko: 이 음식은 약간의 가미만 더하면 완성돼요.
examples.en: This dish will be complete with just a little extra seasoning.
They added a modern touch to the traditional music.
The salt was overdone, so it's too salty.

examples.ko: 새 메뉴는 매운맛의 가미로 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The new menu became popular thanks to a touch of spiciness.

examples.ko: 감정의 가미 없이 사실만 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me only the facts, without adding emotion.

examples.ko: 약간의 유머 가미가 발표를 더 재미있게 만들어요.
examples.en: A bit of humor makes the presentation more fun.

explain: '가미'는 음식, 글, 음악에 다른 것을 조금 더해서 맛이나 분위기를 바꿀 때 써요. 많이 섞는다기보다 살짝 더하는 느낌이에요. 보통 '가미하다'나 '~를 가미한' 모양으로 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The presentation had a bit of humor added, so it was fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~를 가미한 + 명사' 모양으로 무엇을 조금 더했는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the pattern '~를 가미한 + noun', it tells what was lightly added.

phrases.en: This song has a touch of jazz mixed in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 조금 더해져 있는 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of something having been lightly added.

phrases.en: I added a little chili powder to the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '가미'에 '-하다'를 붙인 동사로, 조금 더한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 가미, meaning to add a little.

explain_en: Adding a small touch, like an ingredient or element (가미하다) 가미 is for adding a small something to food, writing, or music to change its flavor or mood. It feels like a light addition, not a heavy mix. It appears more often as 가미하다 or ~를 가미한.

examples.ko: 고압 전기선에는 가까이 가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not go near high-voltage power lines.

examples.ko: 이 탱크 안에는 고압 가스가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This tank contains high-pressure gas.
I cleaned the car with a pressure washer.
I bought a hose that sprays water at high pressure.
At the factory, they handle high-pressure equipment carefully.

examples.ko: 압력솥 안은 고압이라서 뚜껑이 잘 안 열려요.
examples.en: Inside a pressure cooker the pressure is high, so the lid is hard to open.

explain: 전기에 쓰면 높은 전압, 가스나 물에 쓰면 높은 압력으로 읽어요. 보통 '고압 전선', '고압 가스'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 반대는 '저압'이에요.

phrases.example: 고압 전선 근처에서는 연을 날리면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not fly a kite near high-voltage power lines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기가 높은 전압으로 흐르는 선을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for power lines carrying electricity at high voltage.

phrases.en: High-voltage current flows through this wire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 전기 이야기를 할 때 '전류'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 전류 (current) when talking about dangerous electricity.

phrases.en: You have to handle high-pressure gas carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가스나 물처럼 압력이 높은 것 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to gas or water to describe something under high pressure.

explain_en: Strong pressure of water, gas or electricity — machines, technical use. 고압 means high voltage for electricity and high pressure for gas or water. It usually sits in front of another noun, as in 고압 전선. The opposite is 저압.
